page: OVHcloud b3-8 is a general-purpose virtual server instance powered by the KVM hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture with 2 dedicated vCPUs from the AMD EPYC processor family running at 2.3 GHz. The hardware configuration includes 2 physical cores with 1 thread per core, 8.0 GB of system memory providing 4.0 GB per core, and 50 GB of local NVMe SSD storage. It also includes one complimentary public IPv4 address.

Benchmark data indicates strong single-core performance, with the stress-ng single-core CPU test and Geekbench single-core score placing in the top 25%. However, multi-core and memory-intensive operations show limitations. The Geekbench multi-core score, Passmark CPU score, and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression fall into the bottom 25%. Memory bandwidth for large blocks is average at 62.95 GB/sec for read and 45.99 GB/sec for write, while static web serving throughput is poor, registering at 2.76 GB/sec.

Given its dedicated CPU allocation and strong single-core performance, the b3-8 is qualitatively cost-efficient for workloads that do not require massive parallelization. It is suited for lightweight general-purpose tasks, text processing, single-threaded applications, and basic development environments. It is less optimal for heavy database operations, multi-threaded software compilation, or complex image processing due to its lower multi-core and memory benchmark ratings.
